newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Spanish bank shows $2.9 million loss/1995.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bank shows $2.9 million loss/1995.

text.p: Spanish Uniban bank, which is to merge with a Moroccan bank, showed a 27.2 million dirhams ($2.9 million) loss in 1995 due mainly to provisions for non-performing debt, a bank official said on Friday.
The bank in 1994 made losses of 44.01 million dirhams ($4.8 million), the bank said on Friday. No figures were available for 1996.
The bank's 1995 results were also published in Moroccan newspapers on Friday after a meeting of its ordinary general assembly earlier this month.
Uniban expects its merger with leading Wafabank to be approved by main shareholders in February, the official said.
Wafabank decided to buy 100 percent of Uniban or more than 2.46 million shares priced at around $28 million.
A dispute between a group of minority shareholders over the share parity and the management was apparently behind the delay in the final approval of the merger, a Casablanca market analyst said.
Wafabank is offering one share in exchange for five shares of Uniban while shareholders wanted one share against four, the analyst said.
The effective absorption of Uniban by Wafabank will take place by end March 1997, a bourse official said.
One of 47 companies listed on the Casablanca market, Uniban was last traded at 120 dirhams.
